debit_pay_findings.cards: personal checking-account Visa/Mastercard debit (general, all Citi consumer card products historically)
debit_pay_findings.limit_note: one payment per debit card per account per day; automated system minimum payment ~$10; cardholder name must match account name (AU allowed, ask primary's name)
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Long-running FlyerTalk wiki thread (117+ pages) confirms consumer bank-issued debit cards (Wells Fargo, Coinbase, PayPal Business Debit MC, Green Dot permanent, H&R Block Emerald, Swagbucks, TopCashback virtual) still work by phone into 2026; poster danpeake (Mar 17 2026) says 'I've made payments to my Citi account using my bank debit card (attached to a personal checking account) without incident.'

debit_pay_findings.cards: commercial debit cards and commercial prepaid debit cards (business-issued)
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Poster libralibra (Mar 15 2026) reports Citi announced effective ~Jan 30 2026 that 'commercial debit cards and commercial prepaid debit cards are no longer allowed payment methods' — restriction is scoped to COMMERCIAL debit, not consumer debit per follow-up replies.

debit_pay_findings.limit_note: phone menu now skips debit/bank-account choice entirely and routes straight to bank-account (ACH) only
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Community synthesis of recent thread pages: a user reports they can no longer pay Citi Costco with a debit card by phone because the automated menu no longer offers the debit option, while the same user could still pay Citi Custom Cash with debit on the same call.

debit_pay_findings.limit_note: same one-per-day-per-card rule as other Citi products
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Same poster who lost debit-pay on Citi Costco confirms Custom Cash still accepted a debit card payment by phone on the same call, implying the restriction is being rolled out per-product rather than account-wide.

Multiple prepaid-debit BINs (TCB 484224, Pathward Mastercard gift cards, Bancorp Visa 542418, Fluz 4204 BIN, SYW eVGC, BeFrugal 43434058) stopped authorizing for Citi debit payment between Sept-Oct 2024; poster yydv called the TCB block 'a huge loss.' Confirms Citi has been progressively tightening which BINs qualify as 'debit' even before the 2026 commercial-debit rule.

debit_pay_findings.cards: general Capital One credit card accounts
debit_pay_findings.limit_note: rollout was account-by-account ('not available on all accounts currently') when first launched
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Doctor Of Credit: Capital One began showing a debit card as an online bill-payment option (previously phone-only); FlyerTalk's 'Does Chase allow CC payment with debit cards?' thread separately names Capital One as one of the '4 known institutions' (with FIA/BofA, Citi, Synchrony) that accept debit-card bill payment historically.

FlyerTalk 'Does Chase allow CC payment with debit cards?' thread: poster lists 'the four known institutions' that accept debit-card bill payment as FIA Card Services (BofA subsidiary), Citi, Capital One, and Synchrony Bank.

debit_pay_findings.issuer: FIA Card Services / Bank of America
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Same thread: one poster lists FIA as a known debit-accepting issuer, but another replies 'FIA didn't seem to allow it when I tried sometime around January' — inconsistent even within the historical record; no 2025/2026 confirmation found in this sweep.

debit_pay_findings.limit_note: no debit-card bill-pay channel found; bank-linked ACH/bill-pay is the only route
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Multiple FlyerTalk threads agree Chase has never been documented to accept a debit card as a credit-card bill payment method; posters warn 'Just leave Chase alone if they'll bite you' and cite account closures tied to unconventional payment sources (money orders, branch cash, alt-payment platforms) per Doctor Of Credit's shutdown-risk writeup.

debit_pay_findings.channel: n/a (ACH from registered bank account only)
debit_pay_findings.evidence: FlyerTalk 'AmEx Bill Payment Method - Debit Card?' thread concludes Amex does not accept a debit card for bill payment; the only non-Amex-card payment route is ACH from a registered checking account (online or by phone).

stopped_accepting.scope: commercial/business debit and commercial prepaid debit cards blocked as a payment method; consumer/personal debit still working per follow-up reports

Citi Costco Anywhere Visa phone-IVR no longer offers a debit-card option at all (menu skips straight to bank account/ACH); other Citi products on the same account (e.g. Custom Cash) still offered debit at time of report — suggests a per-product rather than per-account rollout
Prepaid/virtual debit BINs delisted in waves: TopCashback (BIN 484224) late Sept 2024, Pathward Mastercard gift cards by Oct 10 2024, Bancorp Visa (BIN 542418) by Oct 23 2024
Cards with BIN prefix 4343 (SYW/Synchrony Year Wood-linked eGift/virtual debit cards) banned wholesale for Citi debit payment

new_card_leads.why_interesting: Invite-only rewards DEBIT card people specifically ask about for pay-by-phone bill payment; FlyerTalk poster confirms 'all earn rewards but amount varies' by product tier

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: Doctor Of Credit's rule: treat 2% cash back as the irreducible opportunity cost floor. True cost = hard fees + forgone 2% baseline; a play only clears if reward value exceeds hard+opportunity cost combined
ms_criteria.why: Prevents chasing a play that looks free on fees alone but loses to a plain 2% card once opportunity cost is counted

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: Heavy spend velocity regardless of ordinary vs manufactured; multiple high-dollar transactions flag risk models more than one large one; especially common on new accounts chasing a bonus threshold
ms_criteria.why: FR usually just freezes/limits rather than closes, but is the first warning sign before a shutdown

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: US Bank and Bank of America/FIA described as fast/aggressive shutdown issuers (BofA closes ALL cards+banking, even IRAs, in one sweep; US Bank flagged as not tolerating MS well, with Elan-brand cards sharing the same ban since Elan is US Bank-owned). Amex tolerant short-term but has long memory (10+ year blacklist). Chase treats alt-payment sources (money orders, branch cash, unusual bill-pay) as an instant red flag across all cards+banking simultaneously.
ms_criteria.why: Community routes high-volume/cash-like spend away from the sensitive issuers and toward more tolerant ones (Amex, some smaller issuers) when possible

ms_criteria.topic: payment-source diversity as a red flag
ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: Citi and Barclays specifically flagged for watching 'unpredictable payments from various debit cards/sources monthly' — paying from many different debit cards/bill-pay sources is itself a shutdown trigger, independent of the underlying spend
ms_criteria.why: Directly relevant to a debit-stacking play: rotating many debit sources to pay one card bill looks like exactly the pattern issuers screen for

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: A single large transaction (e.g. one $10k charge) is viewed as safer than multiple smaller transactions (e.g. two $5k charges) hitting close together, since risk algorithms weight transaction-count/frequency more heavily than raw dollar total
ms_criteria.why: Informs how a big Costco gold buy should be split (or not split) across a billing cycle

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: Rough re-approval windows cited by community: Capital One ~180 days, US Bank ~1 year, Citi ~2 years minimum, Chase disputed (earliest ~14 months, premium cards harder), Amex 10+ years or never
ms_criteria.why: Feeds into whether a shutdown risk is 'tolerable' (short cooldown) vs a career-ending mistake for that issuer

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: The Citi debit-pay wiki thread (117+ pages, 2015-2026) is essentially a running log of which prepaid/virtual debit BINs still authorize; community treats any given BIN as temporary and expects issuers to delist them in batches (documented waves in Jan 2024, Sept-Oct 2024, and the Jan 2026 commercial-debit rule)
ms_criteria.why: Sets the expectation that ANY debit-pay channel found today should be assumed to have a shelf life, not treated as permanent infrastructure

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: Doctor Of Credit maintains a curated list of 'Essential Blogs & Forums' the community treats as required reading for MS, effectively naming itself plus FlyerTalk's Manufactured Spending forum as the primary sources
ms_criteria.why: Confirms doctorofcredit.com + flyertalk.com/forum/manufactured-spending are the community's own top two sources — validates this sweep's beat

gold_costco_notes.note: FlyerTalk 'Shutdown Thread (2025 onwards)': poster hotpancakes (2025-01-10) asked 'any word on shutdowns from buying gold bars @ Costco?' — no one supplied a confirmed shutdown data point in reply; thread drifted to unrelated Chase Pay-Over-Time discussion, so the question remains open/unanswered in the community as of this sweep

Older (2011-era) FlyerTalk 'Buying gold coins/bars with CC' thread: posters describe reselling 1oz gold coins/bars '$35-45 over spot' as the arbitrage mechanic, but also note online bullion dealers charge ~3% MORE if paying by credit card (i.e. the CC premium eats into the arbitrage) and that some card issuers have 'preemptively cut off' gold/bullion purchases — this issuer-level pre-blocking risk is the closest historical precedent found to a Costco-specific gold shutdown

No FlyerTalk or Doctor Of Credit thread found that discusses Costco's warehouse MCC 5300 coding specifically in the context of bullion/gold purchases, nor any 2025-2026 thread confirming a shutdown tied specifically to Costco gold-bar spend — this remains an evidence gap in the community record as of 2026-09-15

taekus_notes.note: FlyerTalk poster asks directly 'Have people used Taekus for pay by phone? Does it earn rewards?' Reply: 'Taekus has personal, business, and corporate cards. All earn rewards but amount varies [by tier].' No confirmation found either way on whether a Citi bill payment via Taekus actually earns Taekus rewards (i.e. whether Citi's payment transaction codes as a 'purchase' on the Taekus side) — unresolved in the thread

Taekus does not appear anywhere on Doctor Of Credit's 'Complete List Of Rewards Earning Debit Cards' page (checked directly) — DoC's own debit-card roundup has no dedicated Taekus review or data as of this sweep, consistent with Taekus being invite-only/low public documentation

Taekus was scheduled for its first public conference appearance at PointsQuest 2025 (NYC, Feb 21-22) with Kat Lin (Taekus COO) as a listed speaker — the community's main non-forum data point on the company, but not a usage data point
